{{Short description|Variable in statistics and risk management}}

'''Buffered probability of exceedance''' ('''bPOE''') is a function of a [[random variable]] used in [[statistics]] and [[risk management]], including [[financial risk]].  The bPOE is the probability of a tail with known mean value <math>x</math>. The figure shows the bPOE at threshold <math>x</math> (marked in red) as the blue shaded area.  Therefore, by definition, bPOE is equal to one minus the confidence level at which the [[Expected shortfall|Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR)]] is equal to <math>x</math>.  bPOE is similar to the [[Frequency of exceedance|probability of exceedance]] of the threshold <math>x</math>, but the tail is defined by its mean rather than the lowest point <math>x</math> of the tail.[[File:BPOE example graph.png|thumb|bPOE shaded in blue for the threshold, x, marked in red.]]

bPOE has its origins in the concept of ''buffered probability of failure (bPOF)'', developed by [[R. Tyrrell Rockafellar]] and [[Johannes Royset]] to measure failure risk.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rockafellar |first1=R. Tyrrell |last2=Royset |first2=Johannes|date=2010 |title=On Buffered Failure Probability in Design and Optimization of Structures |journal=Reliability Engineering and System Safety |volume=95 |issue=5 |pages=499–510 |doi=10.1016/j.ress.2010.01.001 |s2cid=1653873 |url=https://sites.math.washington.edu/~rtr/papers/rtr211-BufferedProb.pdf}}</ref>  It was further developed and defined as the inverse CVaR by Matthew Norton, Stan Uryasev, and Alexander Mafusalov.<ref name="norton1">{{cite journal |last1=Norton |first1=Matthew |last2=Uryasev |first2=Stan |year=2018 |title=Maximization of AUC and Buffered AUC in binary classification |url=http://uryasev.ams.stonybrook.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Maximization-of-AUC-and-Buffered-AUC-in-binary-classification.pdf |journal=Mathematical Programming |publisher=Springer |volume=174 |issue=1–2 |pages=575–612 |doi=10.1007/s10107-018-1312-2 |s2cid=254145122 |access-date=2023-03-12}}</ref><ref name="mafusalov">{{cite journal |last1=Mafusalov |first1=Alexander |last2=Uryasev |first2=Stan|date=2018 |title=Buffered Probability of Exceedance: Mathematical Properties and Optimization |journal=SIAM Journal on Optimization |volume=95 |issue=5 |pages=1077–1103|doi=10.1137/15M1042644 |url=http://uryasev.ams.stonybrook.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/Buffered_probability_of_exceedance.pdf}}</ref> Similar to CVaR, bPOE ==Formal definition==
There are two slightly different definitions of bPOE, so called '''Lower bPOE''' and '''Upper bPOE'''.

For a random variable, <math>X</math> the Lower bPOE,<ref name="norton1" /><ref name="mafusalov" />  <math>\bar{p}_x(X)</math>, at threshold <math>x \in [E[X], \sup X ]</math> is given by:

<math>\bar{p}_x (X) = \min_{a \geq 0} E[ a(X-x) +1 ]^+ = \min_{\gamma <x} \frac{ E[X - \gamma]^+ } { x - \gamma}</math>

where <math>[\cdot]^+ = \max\{\cdot , 0\}</math>. 

bPOE<ref name="mafusalov" /> can be expressed as the [[inverse function]] of CVaR:

<math> \bar{p}_x (X) =  \{ 1 - \alpha | \bar{q}_\alpha (X) = x \} </math>,

where <math>\bar{q}_\alpha (X)</math> is the CVaR of <math>X</math> with confidence level <math>\alpha</math>.
